about: The Magníficat is Mary's canticle from the Gospel according to Saint Luke (Luke 1:46–55), sung at Roman Vespers. This edition preserves the traditional Latin text and its ten numbered biblical verses, followed separately by the Glory Be doxology.

fn.w001: The predicate whose subject is “ánima” (w002) and object is “Dóminum” (w004).

seg.tr: And my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior.

fn.w011: A substantival adjective agreeing with “Deo”: God as my Savior.

seg.tr: For he has regarded the lowliness of his handmaid: behold, from now on all generations will call me blessed.

fn.w013: Introduces the reason for Mary's rejoicing.
fn.w015: Object of “respéxit.” Greek ταπείνωσις confirms the handmaid's low estate here, not praise of her own moral achievement.
fn.w017: Relates the handmaid to God, the understood subject of “respéxit.”
fn.w021: With “ex,” forms the temporal expression “from now on.”
fn.w026: Subject of future “dicent”. It means generations, not nations.

seg.tr: For he who is mighty has done great things for me, and holy is his name.

fn.w029: Dative of advantage: great things done to or for Mary.
fn.w030: A substantival neuter plural adjective, object of “fecit.”
fn.w031: The understood subject of “fecit,” characterized by “potens est.”
fn.w035: Predicate to an understood “est,” agreeing with “nomen.”
fn.w037: Genitive referring to God, who has done the great things.

seg.tr: And his mercy is from generation to generation for those who fear him.

fn.w039: Subject of the clause with an understood copula “is.”
fn.w044: With `a progénie`, forms the expression of mercy extending through successive generations.
fn.w045: A substantival participle in the dative, naming those toward whom mercy extends.

seg.tr: He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the thoughts of their hearts.

fn.w048: Object of “Fecit”: literally wrought or showed strength.
fn.w050: Instrumental ablative with “in,” an image of God's powerful action.
fn.w051: Relates the arm to God, the subject of “Fecit.”
fn.w054: Ablative of respect or sphere: pride is located in the thought of the heart.
fn.w056: The Latin singular is distributive: the heart belongs to each of the proud. Greek αὐτῶν explicitly confirms the plural referent, not God's heart.

seg.tr: He has brought the mighty down from their throne and exalted the lowly.

fn.w060: Ablative after “de,” the seat from which the mighty are brought down.
fn.w063: A substantival adjective contrasted with the mighty.

seg.tr: He has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty.

fn.w066: A substantival adjective in the ablative of content or filling.
fn.w070: Predicative to “dívites”: the rich are sent away empty.

seg.tr: He has helped Israel, his servant, remembering his mercy.

fn.w071: In this biblical context it means coming to Israel's aid. Greek ἀντελάβετο confirms active help.
fn.w073: Apposition to “Israël”. Greek παῖς confirms “servant,” not “boy.”
fn.w075: Perfect participle of a deponent verb. Its passive form has active meaning and refers to God.
fn.w077: Relates mercy to God. Unlike “sui” in s06, it does not refer to the proud.

seg.tr: As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed forever.

fn.w078: Connects the help and remembered mercy with God's earlier promise.
fn.w079: A deponent participle with “est” (w080): passive form, active meaning.
fn.w084: The biblical name used indeclinably in the dative, parallel to “sémini.”
fn.w086: Dative singular. The collective noun denotes Abraham's descendants.

seg.tr: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.
As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

fn.w098: Imperfect indicative with the understood subject “glória.”
